headline: Suspended 4th&1 LLC, 7 Muskeego Street, for five days with two served; approved several liquor license transfers and changes.
summary: Approved one-day entertainment and common victualer licenses, a package store malt and wine license, and several license changes. Found a violation at 4th&1 LLC, 7 Muskeego Street, and issued a five-day suspension with two days served. Continued the Seabra Restaurant item to December and postponed two other items to October 8, 2026.
decisions: Approved the minutes of September 10, 2026, by a 3-0 roll call vote.
Approved a one-day entertainment license for the Pleasant Street Peace Park Fest, 3-0.
Approved a common victualer license for Queiroz Meat Market, 11 Suffolk Street, 3-0.
Approved a change of officers/directors/stock interest for OM Harsh Corp dba A&B Liquors, 110 McKeon Road, 3-0.
Approved an amendment to the hours for Eddy’s Pub and Sports Bar, 120 Stafford Street, 3-0.
Approved a change of manager for SRG Restaurant of Worcester LLC, 229 Grove Street, 3-0.
Approved a change of officers/directors for Interstate Management Company, LLC (dba Hampton Inn & Suites), 65 Prescott Street, 3-0.
Approved a package store malt & wine license for Metro Convenience Inc., 27 Shrewsbury Street, 3-0.
Approved the transfer of the restaurant all alcohol license, common victualer license, and entertainment license for North Worcester Ventures, LLC, dba Greendale’s Pub, 404 West Boylston Street, 3-0.
Filed the entertainment license request from Paku Paku, Inc., 215 Chandler Street, with no action taken, 3-0.
Filed the change of manager request from Italian American World War Veterans of the US Inc. Post 3, 14 Itam Court, with no action taken, 3-0.
Filed the status hearing on failure to file amendment paperwork for Italian American World War Vets of The US, 14 Itam Court, with no action taken, 3-0.
Continued the Seabra Restaurant, 333 Pleasant Street, item to the first meeting in December, 3-0.
Filed the status item for The Broadway, 100 Water Street, 3-0.
Postponed the item for Hinoelia Rivera dba El Coqui Liquor, 184 Chandler Street, to the October 8, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Postponed the item for Carlow Clove, Inc. dba O’Connor’s Restaurant & Bar, 1160 West Boylston Street, to the October 8, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Found by a 3-0 vote that the violation occurred for 4th&1 LLC, 7 Muskeego Street.
Issued a five-day suspension with two days served for 4th&1 LLC, 7 Muskeego Street, 3-0, with the dates October 15, 26, 2026.

plain_text:
License Commission 
         Meeting Minutes 
   SEPTEMBER 24, 2026  
 
 
Attendance: 
 
Commissioners 
Present: 
 
 
Anthony Vigliotti, Chair 
Charran Fisher, Commissioner 
Maritza Cruz, Commissioner 
 
Commissioners 
Absent: 
 
Staff Present: 
 
 
 
Sgt. Thomas Needham, Worcester Police Department  
Officer Patrick Harrington, Worcester Police Department 
Amanda Moran, Law Department 
Inspector Lauren Martin 
Deborah Steele, Licensing  
 
 
 
     
 
 
Call to Order – 10:00 A.M. 
            
Minutes: September 10, 2026 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3 -0 to approve the minutes of September 10, 
2026. 
 
One Day Liquor & Entertainment Requests 
 
1. Worcester Common Ground Inc. & Pleasant Street Business Association, Pleasant 
Street Peace Park Fest 
Request for entertainment license for bands, live performers  
• Saturday-October 3, 2025- 10:00 a.m.-2:00 p.m.
A. Jimenez, participating remotely, stated that this is for a small art market that will be held 
on Pleasant Street and will only go on for a few hours. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day entertainment license. 
List of Exhibits:  Application for one -day entertainment license received and dated August 19, 
2026. 
Common Victualer Requests 
 
2. Queiroz Meat Market, 11 Suffolk Street 
• Sunday Operating Hours* 
• 7:00 AM - 5:00 PM 
• Monday Operating Hours* 
• 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM 
• Tuesday Operating Hours* 
• 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM 
• Wednesday Operating Hours* 
• 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM 
• Thursday Operating Hours* 
• 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM 
• Friday Operating Hours* 
• 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM 
• Saturday Operating Hours* 
• 7:00 AM - 9:00 PM 
 
Bruna Queiroz, participating remotely, stated that  she is  looking to apply for a common 
victualer license. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the common 
victualer license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for common victualer license received and dated September 17, 
2026. 
 
Alcohol/Entertainment Requests 
 
3. OM Harsh Corp dba A&B Liquors, 110 McKeon Road 
• Request for change of officers/directors/stock interest 
 
Attorney John Mooradian, participating remotely, stated that the store is looking to do a 
change of officers/directors and change of stock. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3- 0 to approve the change of 
officers/directors/stock interest.
List of Exhibits:  Application for change of officers/directors/stock interest received and dated 
August 13, 2026. 
 
4. Eddy’s Pub and Sports Bar, 120 Stafford Street 
• Request to amend hours 
 
Gabriel Cardoso appeared upon behalf of the application and stated that he is looking to 
amend his hours so he can open on Tuesdays also. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the amendment to the hours. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for change of hours received and dated September 17, 2026. 
 
5. SRG Restaurant of Worcester LLC, 229 Grove Street 
• Request for change of manager 
 
Jeff Charloff and Juan Fleitas Quinonez, participated remotely. Mr. Charloff stated that he 
is looking to change the manager to Mr. Quinonez. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the change of manager. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for change of manager received and dated September 3, 2026. 
  
6. Interstate Management Company, LLC (dba Hampton Inn & Suites), 65 Prescott 
Street 
• Request for change of officers/directors 
 
Kellie Keating, participating remotely, stated that the hotel is looking to change the 
officers/directors. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the change of officers/directors. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for change of officers/directors received and dated August 3, 2026. 
 
7. Metro Convenience Inc. 27 Shrewsbury Street 
• Request for package store malt & wine license  
 
Ashleigh Santa Maria appeared upon behalf of the application. 
 
Chair Vigliotti stated that the Commission members had viewed the site prior to the meeting. 
 
Ms. Santa Maria presented an overview of her request and list of population changes in the 
area. 
 
No public comment on item.
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3- 0 to approve the package store malt & wine 
license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for package store malt & wine license received and dated July 29, 
2026. 
 
8. North Worcester Ventures, LLC, dba Greendale’s Pub 404 West Boylston Street 
• Request for transfer of restaurant all alcohol license from KJN, Inc. dba Greendale’s 
Pub 
• Request for common victualer license 
• Request for entertainment license for jukebox, tv, radio, dancing by patrons, 
recorded music, amplification system, light show, karaoke, live music 
 
Attorney Robert Hennigan along with the applicants appeared upon behalf of the 
applications. Mr. Hennigan stated that they are looking to transfer the licenses. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3- 0 to approve the transfer of the restaurant all 
alcohol license, common victualer license and entertainment license. 
 
List of Exhibits: 
 
Exhibit A:  Application for transfer of restaurant all alcohol license received and dated 
September 8, 2026. 
Exhibit B: Application for common victualer license received and dated September 8, 2026. 
Exhibit C: Application for entertainment license received and dated September 8, 2026. 
 
9. Paku Paku, Inc., 215 Chandler Street 
Request for entertainment license for tv, amplification system, karaoke, DJ -Filed no 
action taken 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to file the item. 
 
10. Italian American World War Veterans of the US Inc. Post 3, 14 Itam Court 
Request for change of manager-Filed no action taken 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to file the item. 
 
Status Hearings 
 
 
11. Italian American World War Vets of The US, 14 Itam Court  
Failure to file amendment paperwork-Filed no action taken 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to file the item. 
 
12. Seabra Restaurant, 333 Pleasant Street
Steven Morgado appeared upon behalf of the item. He stated that he has been working with 
the owner of  the building to close out some permits, but they have not been completed yet. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3- 0 to continue the item to the first meeting in 
December. 
 
13. The Broadway, 100 Water Street —-Status of paperwork/status of plumbing 
inspection- 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to file the item. 
 
14. Hinoelia Rivera dba El Coqui Liquor, 184 Chandler Street 
 
Upon a roll call  vote the Commission voted 3-0 to postpone the item to the October 8, 2026, 
License Commission meeting. 
 
15. Carlow Clove, Inc. dba O’Connor’s Restaurant & Bar, 1160 West Boylston Street 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to postpone the item to the  October 8, 2026, 
License Commission meeting. 
 
 
Violation Hearings 
 
16. 4th&1 LLC, 7 Muskeego Street 
Violation of Rules #14, #18, 204 CMR 4.03 (2) 
 
Robert Ginisi appeared to answer to the violation and waived his right to counsel. 
Sgt. Needham presented the following: 
On July 31, 2026, members of the Alcohol Enforcement Team visited the Licensed Premises to 
carry out a compliance check following a social media post regarding a “Happy Hour” violation. 
Upon entering, the team observed that the door was unlocked and there were no staff members 
checking IDs, suggesting that the establishment was open to the public. The team engaged with the 
bartender, who subsequently contacted the owner, Robert Ginisi, to come to the premises. While 
waiting for him to arrive, the team asked the bartender about the club’s membership and guest 
documentation. She directed them to a screen on the cash register, where she displayed a list of 
names and explained that she manages a “tab” with the names of customers who are members. 
Upon further questioning about guest documentation, she indicated that the system does not 
record guest names. When asked about the advertised Happy Hour special, she clarified that 
members pay a regular, lower price, while non-members are charged the original price. 
 Mr. Ginisi eventually arrived at the licensed premises and was informed about the identified 
violations. 
Mr. Ginisi stated that he has been at location for nine years and of the time they are a members 
club and the members are allowed to have guests. He stated in nine years there have been no
violations except one minor problem during COVID. He stated that moving forward they will 
raise money to put in a buzzer. He stated they will have a member book for people to sign in. Mr. 
Ginisi stated that when he found out about the Happy Hour posting it was immediately removed. 
He stated that he has seen other clubs do that type of posting so they thought it was okay. 
Mr. Ginisi stated that they stopped doing the member book sign in as they were using the POS 
sale system. Chair Vigliotti stated that system isn’t working.  
Commissioner Fisher  stated that she recalled the violation from 2021 and the Commission had 
reviewed with Mr. Ginisi the club requirements.  
Chair Vigliotti recommend that Mr. Ginisi sit down with the police and Inspectional Services and 
review the club requirements.  
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the violation did occur. 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to issue a five-day suspension with two days 
served, October 15, 26, 2026. 
List of Exhibits:  Police report dated August 24, 2026 
 
Communications 
 
Lissette Ramos vs ABCC communication -filed 
 
Adjournment 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted to adjourn the meeting at 11:01 a.m.
